disclaimer: Information only. This directory is never financial, legal, or tax advice. Always confirm details on the official source website before you act.

scam_warning.headline: Real unclaimed money programs are free. Walk away from anyone who charges you.
rules: Never pay a finder, locator, or 'asset recovery' fee to reach money on this list. Claiming from a state, federal, or industry-run database costs nothing or only the government's own fees.
If a company contacts you out of the blue about 'found money', you do not need them. You can search every database in this directory yourself, on your own, in minutes.
Unsolicited callers, texts, or emails asking for your Social Security number, bank login, or an upfront payment are scams. Hang up, delete, and search the official site yourself.
Verify the address bar: official government searchers end in .gov. State officers and the industry associations listed here are named on each card.
In most states, licensed finders may legally take 10-35% of your money as a commission - yet the exact same claim filed directly with the state is free. Everything here is the direct path.
No card in this directory is an affiliate link. We are paid nothing by any program listed.

core_documents.headline: Documents to gather before you start
items: Photo ID (driver's license or passport) for yourself, and for a deceased owner a death certificate
Every last name, first name, and middle initial the owner may have used, plus any maiden or former names
Every address the owner lived at in the state you are searching - claim forms ask for these
Last four digits of the owner's Social Security number (you type it on the official claim form only; a lookup site asking your full SSN just to search is a scam signal)
For a deceased owner: proof you are the executor, heir, or administrator, plus the probate paperwork your state requests
For businesses or organizations: registration documents and proof of your authority to sign
A pen and a place to keep claim reference numbers - you may file several claims in one sitting

finders.name: NAUPA state-by-state official map
finders.jurisdiction: All US states + DC (via each state office)
finders.operator: National Association of Unclaimed Property Administrators (NAUPA), the official association of state unclaimed-property officers
finders.what_it_finds: The official starting point for the state database that holds forgotten bank accounts, uncashed payroll and dividend checks, insurance payouts, utility deposits, stocks, safe-deposit-box contents, and credit balances in the owner's name. Every state runs its own free search.
docs_ready: Prior addresses in the state (claims are filed with each state where the property sat)
Name variations and former names
Photo ID and Social Security number for the claim form
For a relative's property: your relationship and their death certificate
finders.tips: Pick your state from the map. Most smaller balances are approved in weeks if your address history is accurate. Searching a name in every state where the person lived is normal - property usually sits in the state of the last known address, not where you live now.

finders.name: MissingMoney.com multi-state search
finders.jurisdiction: Most participating US states in one search
finders.operator: NAUPA-endorsed central search covering most participating state databases
finders.what_it_finds: Several dozen state unclaimed-property databases at once: dormant checking and savings accounts, uncashed checks, refunds, security deposits, and small stock holdings reported by banks and employers to the states.
docs_ready: Photo ID for each owner (including joint owners)
Address history for the owner
Your Social Security number for the claim form
finders.tips: It does not cover every state, so also check your state's own site through the NAUPA map. Searching twice (here and on your state site) takes minutes and costs nothing.

finders.name: Indiana Unclaimed Property search
finders.operator: Indiana Attorney General's Unclaimed Property Division
finders.what_it_finds: Money and property reported to Indiana: dormant accounts, uncashed wages, insurance proceeds, utility and landlord deposits, and safe-deposit-box contents for Indiana addresses.
docs_ready: Photo ID
Social Security number
Address that matches the reported property
Death certificate and proof of heirship for a relative's claim
finders.tips: Claims are free and can be filed online. If the name search shows nothing, try the maiden name, initials, or a MISS/MISS- spelling the reporting company may have used.

finders.name: California Unclaimed Property search
finders.what_it_finds: Forgotten bank accounts, uncashed checks, stocks, mutual funds, insurance proceeds, and safe-deposit contents held for California owners.
docs_ready: Photo ID
Address history for the owner
Social Security number
Probate or heirship documents for deceased owners
finders.tips: Search is free; download-and-mail claim forms are the normal path for larger amounts.

finders.name: Texas Unclaimed Property search
finders.what_it_finds: Dormant accounts, uncashed payroll and vendor checks, mineral and royalty proceeds, insurance benefits, and court-held money reported to Texas.
docs_ready: Photo ID
Social Security number
For estates: letters testamentary or a small-estate affidavit as Texas requires
finders.tips: File online for free. Oil and gas royalty claims are common here - bring lease or deed info if the property traces to land.

finders.name: New York Unclaimed Funds search
finders.operator: New York State Office of the State Comptroller
finders.what_it_finds: Dormant savings and checking accounts, uncashed checks, insurance benefits, escrow balances, and stock reported to New York State.
docs_ready: Photo ID
Social Security number
Address history
For deceased owners: death certificate plus documents proving your authority
finders.tips: Claims are free at any time. Beware letter offers to 'recover' New York funds for a percentage - filing yourself through the Comptroller costs nothing.

finders.name: Florida Unclaimed Property search
finders.what_it_finds: Dormant accounts, uncashed checks, dormant school and bank accounts, unclaimed insurance and utility deposits held by Florida.
docs_ready: Photo ID
Social Security number
For deceased owners: death certificate and proof of kinship
finders.tips: Payments are free and can be electronic. There is a known pattern of paid finders advertising Florida 'Treasure Hunt' balances - the state site is the free source.

finders.name: PBGC Missing Participants search
finders.operator: Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation (PBGC), a US federal agency
finders.what_it_finds: Your own unclaimed retirement benefit in a private-sector pension plan that ended among tens of thousands of participants the plan could not locate - guaranteed lifetime payments, not a one-time check.
docs_ready: Full legal name and any name changes
Social Security number
Dates and names of employers you (or the late plan member) worked for
Government ID for identity verification
finders.tips: Searching is free and takes minutes. Never let anyone take a cut of a pension you can locate here yourself.

finders.name: DOL abandoned retirement plan search
finders.operator: US Department of Labor, Employee Benefits Security Administration (EBSA)
finders.what_it_finds: Participation in a workplace 401(k) or pension plan reported to EBSA when the company closed and left a plan abandoned - with contacts for the institution now holding the assets.
docs_ready: Employer name and dates of employment
Any old benefit statements or Form W-2s you kept
Social Security number
finders.tips: Also free: EBSA's benefits advisors take calls at 1-866-444-3272 (the federal line is free to call; it is the US Department of Labor, not a finder).

finders.name: FDIC unclaimed deposits search
finders.jurisdiction: US federally insured banks placed in receivership
finders.operator: Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), a US federal agency
finders.what_it_finds: Your un-insured-or-unclaimed deposit or dividend in a failed bank: money the FDIC is still holding, and any account interest owed, with the mail-in or online claim route.
docs_ready: Photo ID
Social Security number or taxpayer ID
Proof of the account (old statement, register, deposit slip) if you have it
Death certificate and authority documents where the owner is deceased
finders.tips: Search first name and last name variations. Claims are free; filing requires mailing ID documents only through the FDIC's own instructions on that page.

finders.name: NCUA unclaimed credit-union deposits search
finders.operator: National Credit Union Administration (NCUA), a US federal agency
finders.what_it_finds: Unclaimed share accounts, share drafts, and dividends in closed credit unions, plus instructions for claiming them through the federal Asset Management and Assistance Center.
docs_ready: Photo ID
Social Security number
Old credit-union statements if you kept any
Proof of authority for a deceased owner's account
finders.tips: Credit-union payouts can include dividend interest, so even a small remembered account is worth a free search.

finders.name: NAIC Life Insurance Policy Locator
finders.jurisdiction: US life insurers reporting to state regulators
finders.operator: National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC), the official association of US state insurance regulators
finders.what_it_finds: A deceased loved one's unclaimed life insurance policy or annuity. Your request goes to member insurers, and any company holding a match contacts you directly and pays you directly - the tool never sees your results and no money changes hands through it.
docs_ready: Deceased person's full legal name
Date of birth and date of death (death certificate helps)
Social Security number for the deceased, if you have it
Your own ID and contact information as the requestor
finders.tips: Free request, no account needed. Results arrive by mail only from the insurer. There is no way to 'search your name' here by design - it is for locating a specific deceased person's policy, so have the paperwork above ready. Also worth one more search: the state insurance department where the person lived.

finders.name: IRS Where's My Refund and undeliverable federal refunds
finders.operator: Internal Revenue Service (IRS), a US federal agency
finders.what_it_finds: A federal income-tax refund that never arrived - an undeliverable check, a refund you were owed but never claimed on a filed return, or a refund the IRS still owes for a year you brought in income and did not file at all because you could still claim it.
docs_ready: Social Security number (or ITIN)
Filing status and exact refund amount expected
Copy of the tax return for the year, or wage statements to file it now
Current address - a change of address you file is what makes a reissued check arrive
finders.tips: You generally have three years from the filing deadline to claim a refund for a year you did not file. Never pay a company a percentage of 'a refund they found for you' - the IRS pays you directly.

finders.name: Treasury Hunt for matured savings bonds
finders.operator: US Department of the Treasury, Bureau of the Fiscal Service
finders.what_it_finds: US savings bonds that reached final maturity but were never cashed, bonds, or bond interest payments the Treasury owes the owner or heirs.
docs_ready: Owner's Social Security number
Owner's full legal name
For deceased owners: death certificate and proof of your right to redeem
Any bond paper certificates you physically find (they may already be replaced electronically here)
finders.tips: Free and instant to search; results are handled by TreasuryDirect. Bonds older than 40 years have stopped earning interest, so cashing promptly makes sense once found.

finders.name: HUD/FHA mortgage insurance premium refund search
finders.operator: US Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), a US federal agency
finders.what_it_finds: An unclaimed FHA upfront mortgage insurance premium refund or share due when a property with FHA financing was sold or the loan was paid off early in certain years.
docs_ready: FHA case number if you have it (it is on the loan closing paperwork)
Name on the loan
Property address
Social Security number
finders.tips: HUD pays refunds itself and warns about third parties taking a cut of these exact refunds. Search is free.
